novelty_flags.label: Theorem 4 (complexity frontier)
novelty_flags.one_line: The direct-versus-recursive architecture comparison omits Greenaway-McGrevy (2013), which derives large-panel MSPE comparisons for direct and recursive multistep forecasts; it does not subsume causal TWSF inference, but it is a necessary nearest comparator for the claimed architecture frontier.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1–4 and the honest_scope restriction
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Selected-layout span/transport recovery, independent auxiliary-block selection, and short-recursion power boundedness are accepted as declared conditional-regime premises rather than derived properties of arbitrary panels.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The feasible selected-path band and variance-share frontier are claims only over the declared class C_n under those recovery, selection, Gaussian-noise, and stability conditions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes pointwise inference and extends TWSF to prespecified linear summaries over a fixed multistep horizon using direct and recursive constructions; it does not state a simultaneous full-path band.
The paper develops simultaneous confidence bands for many functional parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores and high-dimensional uniform CLTs.
The paper gives covariance comparisons and anti-concentration for maxima of Gaussian vectors without covariance restrictions, plus a multiplier-CLT application.
The paper studies fixed-design error-in-variables PCR, minimum-norm identification, and nonasymptotic out-of-sample prediction guarantees.
The paper constructs residual-bootstrap confidence intervals for treatment effects at every treated unit and post-treatment time in interactive-fixed-effects panels.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 109(507), 2014, pp. 1054–1070
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies adaptive nonparametric regression confidence bands and establishes lower bounds under its nonparametric coverage criteria.
The paper compares conventional recursive and direct multistep forecasts in panel VARs through asymptotic MSPE expressions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) and the direct-versus-iterated forecasting literature to related work, then state precisely why an MSPE comparison neither delivers the TWSF Gaussian-complexity frontier nor the simultaneous-band result.

Promote the sharp-horizon question into a sharper comparator-facing result by identifying the first recursive perturbation term that governs the exponent and constructing a matching legal failure family.
Add a boundary corollary comparing the proposed multiplier ribbon to Bonferroni and to the fixed-horizon Shen interval on the H_n=1 embedding, with an explicit critical-value-rate contrast.

recommended_next_step: Revise the architecture-frontier literature positioning and explicit non-subsumption comparison, then advance the field-tier selected-path kernel to Stage 0.
